content.prompt: Square numbers

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}3^{2}&=3\times3\\&=9\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}5^{2}&=5\times5\\&=25\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Each side of these triangles has been measured.

spec.description: Unshaded 3–4–5 triangle with a bottom-left right angle and internal numeral 1.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (0,0), (4,0), (0,3); side lengths 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All measurements, the right-angle marker and numeral are permanent student-visible givens.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with base 7.5 cm, right vertical side 4 cm, diagonal 8.5 cm, bottom-right right angle and internal numeral 2.

spec.answerVisibility: All measurements, the right-angle marker and numeral are permanent student-visible givens.

spec.description: Unshaded non-right triangle with horizontal 8 cm base, left side 5.4 cm, right side 7.5 cm, apex left of the base midpoint and internal numeral 4. No right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: Base endpoints (0,0), (8,0); apex x=(8²+5.4²−7.5²)/(2×8), y=√(5.4²−x²). The coordinates are construction values, not additional student givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All measurements and the numeral are permanent student-visible givens; no inferred angle or calculation is printed.

answer.worked:
The shorter sides are $3$ cm and $4$ cm; the longest side is $5$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=3^2=9\\b^2&=4^2=16\\a^2+b^2&=9+16=25\\c^2&=5^2=25\end{align*}$$
Lengths are in cm and squared values are in cm². Interchanging $a$ and $b$ also gives a correct row.

The shorter sides are $4$ cm and $7.5$ cm; the longest side is $8.5$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=4^2=16\\b^2&=7.5^2=56.25\\a^2+b^2&=16+56.25=72.25\\c^2&=8.5^2=72.25\end{align*}$$
Lengths are in cm and squared values are in cm². Interchanging $a$ and $b$ also gives a correct row.

The shorter sides are $2.5$ cm and $6$ cm; the longest side is $6.5$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=2.5^2=6.25\\b^2&=6^2=36\\a^2+b^2&=6.25+36=42.25\\c^2&=6.5^2=42.25\end{align*}$$
Lengths are in cm and squared values are in cm². Interchanging $a$ and $b$ also gives a correct row.

The shorter sides are $5.4$ cm and $7.5$ cm; the longest side is $8$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=5.4^2=29.16\\b^2&=7.5^2=56.25\\a^2+b^2&=29.16+56.25=85.41\\c^2&=8^2=64\end{align*}$$
Lengths are in cm and squared values are in cm². Here $a^2+b^2\ne c^2$. Interchanging $a$ and $b$ also gives a correct row.

answer.worked:
$a=9$, $b=12$, $c=15$.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=9^2+12^2\\a^2+b^2&=81+144\\a^2+b^2&=225\\c^2&=15^2\\c^2&=225\end{align*}$$

$a=5$, $b=7$, $c=9$.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=5^2+7^2\\a^2+b^2&=25+49\\a^2+b^2&=74\\c^2&=9^2\\c^2&=81\end{align*}$$

$a=4$, $b=5$, $c=9$.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=4^2+5^2\\a^2+b^2&=16+25\\a^2+b^2&=41\\c^2&=9^2\\c^2&=81\end{align*}$$
Since $41\ne81$, the numbers do not form a Pythagorean triad.

$a=7$, $b=24$, $c=25$.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+b^2&=7^2+24^2\\a^2+b^2&=49+576\\a^2+b^2&=625\\c^2&=25^2\\c^2&=625\end{align*}$$
Since $a^2+b^2=c^2$, the numbers form a Pythagorean triad.

content.prompt: $(18,30,n)$ is a Pythagorean triad. Find the value(s) of $n$.

answer.short: $n=24$ only. Taking $n$ as the largest number gives $\sqrt{1224}$, which is not a whole number.
answer.worked:
If $30$ is the largest number:
$$\begin{align*}18^2+n^2&=30^2\\n^2&=30^2-18^2\\n^2&=900-324\\n&=\sqrt{576}=24\end{align*}$$
If $n$ is the largest number:
$$\begin{align*}18^2+30^2&=n^2\\n^2&=324+900\\n&=\sqrt{1224}\end{align*}$$
Since $34^2<1224<35^2$, $\sqrt{1224}$ is not a whole number. Therefore, $n=24$ is the only answer.

inlines.text: Oliver holds the end of the string of a kite 1.2 m above the ground.

Find the height of the kite above the ground.

spec.description: Oliver at the lower left holds a string leading to a kite at the upper right. The horizontal leg begins at hand height. The dashed vertical extends from the kite to the ground, while a separate dimension h measures the full height.
spec.mathematics: The right triangle has hypotenuse 30 m and horizontal leg 18 m. Its vertical leg excludes the 1.2 m hand height. The full height h includes that additional 1.2 m. Diagram proportions follow the source schematic rather than a scale construction.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the vertical distance from Oliver’s hand to the kite. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}
x^2+18^2&=30^2\\
x^2+324&=900\\
x^2&=576\\
x&=\sqrt{576}\\
x&=24.
\end{align*}$$
Add the height of Oliver’s hand:
$$\begin{align*}
h&=24+1.2\\
h&=25.2\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the base, so each half is $12\div2=6\text{ cm}$.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other. The upper right triangle therefore has perpendicular sides $10.3\text{ cm}$ and $8.5\text{ cm}$.

answer.worked:
The vertical side of the upper right triangle is $18-4=14\text{ cm}$.

spec.mathematics: Equal sides 15.2 cm, altitude 8.6 cm, full base w.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and w are visible.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the base.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{w}{2}&=\sqrt{15.2^2-8.6^2}\\\frac{w}{2}&=\sqrt{157.08}\\w&=2\sqrt{157.08}\\w&\approx25.07\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: Parallel horizontal sides 18.2 cm and 23.1 cm; left sloping side 10.2 cm; height a.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and a are visible.

answer.worked:
Draw a perpendicular from the top-left vertex to the base. The small right triangle has horizontal side $23.1-18.2=4.9\text{ cm}$ and vertical side $a$.
$$\begin{align*}a&=\sqrt{10.2^2-4.9^2}\\a&=\sqrt{80.03}\\a&\approx8.95\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Trapezium with vertical left side and two left right-angle marks; no internal construction is supplied.
spec.mathematics: Height 15.4 cm, top 3.2 cm, sloping right side 22.6 cm, full base p.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and p are visible.

answer.worked:
Draw a perpendicular from the top-right vertex to the base. Let the horizontal side of the resulting right triangle be $b$.
$$\begin{align*}b&=\sqrt{22.6^2-15.4^2}\\b&=\sqrt{273.6}\\p&=3.2+\sqrt{273.6}\\p&\approx19.74\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Kite with external side-length dimensions, dashed perpendicular diagonals, single ticks on left sides, double ticks on right sides and triple ticks on the vertical half-diagonals. The 19 cm dimension spans the full vertical diagonal; y spans the full horizontal diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Left equal sides 10.5 cm, right equal sides 16.8 cm, bisected vertical diagonal 19 cm; find horizontal diagonal y.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and y are visible. A white label mask preserves the legibility of the bottom dimension label.

answer.worked:
Each half of the vertical diagonal is $19\div2=9.5\text{ cm}$. Let the left and right horizontal segments be $u$ and $v$.
$$\begin{align*}u&=\sqrt{10.5^2-9.5^2}\\u&=\sqrt{20}\\v&=\sqrt{16.8^2-9.5^2}\\v&=\sqrt{191.99}\\y&=\sqrt{20}+\sqrt{191.99}\\y&\approx18.33\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
The diagonal of a rectangle is 10 cm long. The rectangle is twice as long as it is wide.
What are the dimensions of the rectangle? Round your answers to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the width in centimetres. The length is $2x$ centimetres.
$$\begin{aligned}x^2+(2x)^2&=10^2\\5x^2&=100\\x^2&=20\\x&=\sqrt{20}\\&\approx4.47\end{aligned}$$
The width is $\sqrt{20}\text{ cm}\approx4.47\text{ cm}$ and the length is $2\sqrt{20}\text{ cm}\approx8.94\text{ cm}$.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height bisects the base, giving a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $10\text{ cm}$ and shorter side $5\text{ cm}$.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height bisects the base, giving a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $x$ and shorter side $\frac{x}{2}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y &= \sqrt{7^2+6^2}\\y &= \sqrt{85}\\x &= \sqrt{14^2+y^2}\\x &= \sqrt{14^2+(\sqrt{85})^2}\\x &= \sqrt{281}\\x &\approx 16.76\end{align*}$$
Thus $y \approx 9.22$ and $x \approx 16.76$, to 2 d.p.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows three circles with centres A, B and C. The circles touch without overlapping.

Show that triangle ABC is right-angled.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, three tangent circles below the stem
spec.description: Unfilled externally tangent circles, with A above, C lower left and B lower right; centre points joined as triangle ABC and external diameter labels retained.
spec.mathematics: Radii A = 6 cm, B = 4 cm and C = 2 cm. Centre distances AB = 10 cm, AC = 8 cm and BC = 6 cm. Coordinates place AC and BC perpendicular without adding a right-angle marker to the question.
spec.answerVisibility: Diameter givens and centre labels are visible; derived distances and the right-angle conclusion are absent.

answer.short: $AC^2+BC^2=8^2+6^2=100=AB^2$. By the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The radii are $6\text{ cm}$, $4\text{ cm}$ and $2\text{ cm}$. Since the circles touch externally, each centre distance is the sum of the two radii.

$$\begin{align*}AB&=6+4=10\text{ cm}\\BC&=4+2=6\text{ cm}\\AC&=6+2=8\text{ cm}\\AC^2+BC^2&=8^2+6^2\\AC^2+BC^2&=100\\AB^2&=10^2=100\end{align*}$$

Thus $AC^2+BC^2=AB^2$. By the converse of Pythagoras’ theorem, triangle ABC is right-angled at C.

content.prompt: Determine the value of $h$ in exact surd form.

spec.description: Nine successive right-angled triangles share a central vertex. The initial radius and all nine outer sides are labelled 1. Every outer junction has a right-angle marker, and the final radius is labelled h.
spec.mathematics: Starting with P0=(1,0), derive Pn=P(n−1)+(-y,x)/sqrt(x²+y²). Each new outer side has length 1 and is perpendicular to the preceding radius. The final radius has squared length 10.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and h are visible; intermediate radii and the final answer appear in controlled answers.

answer.worked:
Each outer unit side is perpendicular to the preceding radius. Let $r_1,\ldots,r_8$ be the successive intermediate radii. Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}
r_1&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\\
r_2&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{3}\\
r_3&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{4}=2\\
r_4&=\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt{5}\\
r_5&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}\\
r_6&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{6})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{7}\\
r_7&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{7})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{8}\\
r_8&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{8})^2+1^2}=\sqrt{9}=3\\
h&=\sqrt{3^2+1^2}=\sqrt{10}
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: JKML is a square. Determine the length of $NK$ if the height of the triangle $\Delta NML$ is 24 cm. Answer to two decimal places.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12, square diagram below the stem on the left
spec.description: Square JKML containing equilateral triangle NML. JN and KN join the upper vertices to N. S is on KM level with N, with NS perpendicular to SK. Retains all six filled point markers, three equal-side ticks and three 60-degree angle labels.
spec.mathematics: For square side s, L=(0,0), M=(s,0), J=(0,s), K=(s,s), N=(s/2,sqrt(3)s/2) and S=(s,sqrt(3)s/2). Triangle NML is equilateral. Diagram coordinates express these relationships without printing additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible; no calculated lengths or solution-only construction is shown.

answer.worked:
Split equilateral triangle $NML$ vertically down the middle. Each resulting right-angled triangle has height 24 cm and base half the side length. Let $NM=x$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}
\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^2+24^2&=x^2\\
\frac{x^2}{4}+24^2&=x^2\\
24^2&=\frac{3x^2}{4}\\
x^2&=768\\
x&=\sqrt{768}
\end{align*}$$
The square has side length $\sqrt{768}$ cm. Also, $SM=24$ cm and $NS$ is half the square's side.
$$\begin{align*}
KS&=KM-SM\\
KS&=\sqrt{768}-24\\
NS&=\frac{\sqrt{768}}{2}\\
NK&=\sqrt{\left(\sqrt{768}-24\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{768}}{2}\right)^2}\\
NK&\approx14.35\text{ cm}
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
A rectangle 5 m by 24 m is cut along a straight line from a corner to an opposite side to make a right-angled triangle and a trapezium.

The two shapes are then rearranged to form a large right-angled triangle.

Determine both possible perimeters of the large right-angled triangle. Round any non-integer answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.short: $60\text{ m}$ or $101.26\text{ m}$. Cut to an opposite-side midpoint and rotate the small triangle through $180^\circ$. The resulting perpendicular sides are $24\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$, or $48\text{ m}$ and $5\text{ m}$; use Pythagoras’ theorem and add the three sides.

inlines.text: Cut from a corner to the midpoint of an opposite side. There are two possibilities. In each case, rotate the small triangle through
about that midpoint and join it to the trapezium. The two equal sloping edges form the hypotenuse of the large triangle.
If the cut ends at the midpoint of a 24 m side, the small triangle has perpendicular sides 12 m and 5 m. The rearranged triangle has perpendicular sides 24 m and 10 m.
If the cut ends at the midpoint of a 5 m side, the small triangle has perpendicular sides 24 m and 2.5 m. The rearranged triangle has perpendicular sides 48 m and 5 m.
Both constructions preserve the original area:

teachingContext.method: Choose the hypotenuse or shorter-side formula.
Identify the right-angled triangle, then substitute into the appropriate formula.
Keep intermediate values exact and round only at the final step.

constructionVerification.method: Coordinate reconstruction with a half-turn about each cut midpoint.
constructionVerification.first: For rectangle vertices (0,0), (24,0), (24,5), (0,5), cut from (0,0) to (12,5). Rotating the small triangle about (12,5) produces the large triangle with vertices (0,0), (24,0), (24,10).
constructionVerification.second: For the same rectangle, cut from (0,0) to (24,2.5). Rotating the small triangle about (24,2.5) produces the large triangle with vertices (0,0), (0,5), (48,5).

Syllabus Content
MA4-PYT-C-01 applies Pythagoras’ theorem to solve problems in various contexts

Identify and define Pythagoras’ theorem
• Identify and describe the hypotenuse as the side opposite the right angle and the longest side in any right-angled triangle
• Establish the relationship between the lengths of the sides of a right-angled triangle
